title: Where Rectified Flows Leak: Characterising Membership Signals Along the Interpolation Path
claim: Probing a model along its interpolation path yields a bell-shaped, step-resolved signal that can be fed to a classifier to detect training membership.
layout: Stacked top-to-bottom: geometric flow diagram, bell curve, then classifier box; arrow left-to-right
description: The figure has three vertically stacked parts. At the top, two tilted parallelogram planes stand for distributions p0 (tan, with scattered dots, labelled Σ0) and p1 (light blue, labelled Σ1). A dashed gray line joins a noise point x0 (orange tick) to a data point x1 (blue tick) through the intermediate point x_λ. A green arrow shows the predicted velocity v_θ(x_λ, λ). It points to a reconstructed x̂1 (green tick), and a dashed double arrow marks the error d between x̂1 and x1. A long black arrow underneath is labelled 'Flow parameter λ'. Below it, a smooth black bell curve is captioned 'λ − Membership Signal'. At the bottom, a pale yellow box labelled 'Membership Inference Attack' contains an MLP funnel that splits into 'Member' and 'Non Member' boxes. The eye goes first to the large distribution labels and the geometric diagram.
caption: Overview of our approach. Top: Detection protocol, given a sample x1, we interpolate with noise x0 at varying λ, predict the velocity vθ(xλ, λ), and measure reconstruction error d = ∥x1 −ˆx1∥2. Middle: The train-test gap in reconstruction error follows a bell-shaped curve over λ; we derive a closed-form expression for the peak location. Bottom: As a proof of concept, the λ-resolved errors can be fed to an MLP classifier to perform Membership Inference Attack.
abstract: Understanding what generative models retain from training data remains challenging, with implications for copyright and privacy. Beyond verbatim reproduction, models can encode subtler traces of their training data that never surface in their outputs yet remain exploitable. We study this regime for Rectified Flows, which are increasingly used in deployed generative systems. We analyse the interpolation path $X_\lambda = (1-\lambda)X_0 + \lambda X_1$ that defines the Rectified Flow training. We show that a gap exists between the reconstruction of train and test data that follows a bell-shaped curve over $\lambda$, wich accumulates during training, while the validation metrics remain stable. The signal has a maximum whose location we derive in closed form under Gaussian assumptions. We validate these predictions on both audio and images and show that the bell-shaped structure is universal, while the peak prediction holds when our assumptions are satisfied. As a proof of concept, we exploit this specific $\lambda$-resolved structure to perform a Membership Inference Attack, distinguishing members of the training set from non-members.
